notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
Build shows one notch drawer frame and one spike sharing the junction of **0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0** — the corner of cell 0,0 (also the corner of 0,1 and 1,0) where the empty cell 1,1 sits.

- **One drawer at the same corner:** `notch:0#1,1#notch2` — `hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf` placed at `1,1 lv0 k2`. This is the notch position between `piece:0,1,0` and `piece:1,0,0` that meets the junction at `47.8,0,82.9`. The frame contains the drawer.
- **One spike at the same corner:** `spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0` at level 0 junction `[{q:0,r:0},{q:0,r:1},{q:1,r:0}]` posMm 47.8,82.9.

Both sit on the same three-cell junction, physically touching (meshClash clear, check_build ok). Three full cells `0,0` `1,0` `0,1` provide the bases to offer both parts. Capped and joint-bolted.

View from above (polar 10) verifies adjacency.
